encounters.cc: Shortness of breath and dry cough for 6 months

lines: Shortness of breath and dry cough for 6 months
A 67-year-old male presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of gradually worsening shortness of breath and a dry cough.
He has a past medical history of hypertension.
He takes for which he takes hydrochlorothiazide.
He is a retired construction worker and has a 30-pack-year smoking history, although he quit smoking 10 years ago.
His oxygen saturation is 92% on room air.
On physical examination, you note fine crackles at the bases of both lungs.
High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the chest shows bilateral subpleural reticular opacities with honeycombing but no evidence of significant lymphadenopathy or pleural effusion.
Pulmonary function tests reveal a restrictive pattern with a forced vital capacity (FVC) of 65% predicted and a reduced diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) of 45% predicted.

encounters.cc: Routine follow-up after hospital discharge for total hip replacement

lines: Routine follow-up after hospital discharge for total hip replacement
The patient is a 67-year-old male with atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis who returns for routine follow-up after hospital discharge for total hip replacement.
Three weeks ago, he underwent total hip replacement surgery following severe osteoarthritis that had caused debilitating pain and immobility.
He denies bleeding, bruising, or black stools.
He notes improved mobility and is working with physical therapy to regain strength.
His surgical recovery has been uncomplicated, and his wound has healed well.
His past medical history includes hypertension, atrial fibrillation, and obesity.
He reports that during his hospital stay, he was started on rivaroxaban to reduce the risk of blood clots.
Since discharge, he has been adherent with his medication, which he takes orally once daily.
Family history is notable for a father who suffered a stroke at age 74.
Social history reveals that he quit smoking 10 years ago and drinks alcohol socially.
Physical examination today is unremarkable, with well-healed surgical scars, stable vital signs, and no edema.

encounters.cc: Concern about a slowly growing lesion on the nose

lines: Concern about a slowly growing lesion on the nose
This 68-year-old male with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis presents with concern about a nasal lesion.
He reports the lesion has been slowly growing over the past year, with occasional bleeding during shaving but is otherwise asymptomatic.
45-pack-year smoking history, although he quit smoking 10 years ago
On physical examination, you note a pearly, flesh-colored papule with telangiectasias on the lateral aspect of his nose.
A biopsy of the lesion is performed, and histopathology reveals nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and retraction artifact.

encounters.cc: Gradually worsening shortness of breath over the past 2 years

lines: Gradually worsening shortness of breath over the past 2 years
The patient is a 70-year-old male with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and atrial fibrillation who returns to Pulmonary and Critical Care with worsening dyspnea.
He reports increasing difficulty climbing stairs and must pause frequently while walking on level ground.
He has noticed frequent coughing spells and unintentional weight loss.
He denies recent upper respiratory symptoms, chest pain, or fever.
- Basal Cell Carcinoma (Nodular type, of nose) (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
Past medical history includes hypertension and seasonal allergies.
He smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years but quit 6 years ago.
On physical examination, he appears thin and is using accessory muscles of respiration.
He breathes through pursed lips and has a barrel-shaped chest.
Percussion of the lungs reveals hyperresonance.
A chest X-ray shows flattened diaphragms and hyperlucent lower lobes.
Pulmonary function tests demonstrate a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio with increased total lung capacity and residual volume.

encounters.cc: Gradually worsening shortness of breath and persistent dry cough

lines: Gradually worsening shortness of breath and persistent dry cough
The patient with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema returns with worsening dyspnea and dry cough.
He states that he becomes winded even with mild exertion, such as carrying groceries or climbing stairs.
He denies chest pain, wheezing, fever, or sputum production.
- Basal Cell Carcinoma (Nodular type, of nose) (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
He smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years but quit 5 years ago.
He worked in a furniture manufacturing plant for 35 years and reports long-term exposure to wood dust and solvents.
Oxygen saturation is 92% on room air.
On physical exam, his lungs reveal fine, end-inspiratory “Velcro-like” crackles at the bases and mild digital clubbing.
Chest x-ray reveals reticular opacities in the lower lobes bilaterally.
High-resolution CT shows subpleural reticulations, traction bronchiectasis, and honeycombing in a basilar distribution.
A lung biopsy is performed and reveals dense fibrosis with temporal heterogeneity and areas of microscopic honeycombing alternating with relatively preserved lung parenchyma.
There are no granulomas or eosinophilic infiltrates.
Pulmonary function tests show a reduced total lung capacity, normal FEV1/FVC ratio, and markedly decreased DLCO.

encounters.cc: Severe dyspnea on exertion and persistent dry cough

lines: Severe dyspnea on exertion and persistent dry cough
He returns for follow-up of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema previously documented in 2020 and 2023.
He reports that he becomes winded just walking from his living room to the kitchen and has difficulty climbing stairs without stopping to rest.
He denies chest pain, wheezing, or sputum production.
He has not had any recent illnesses or exposure to toxic fumes.
- Basal Cell Carcinoma (Nodular type, of nose) (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
His medical history is significant only for well-controlled hypertension.
He smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years but quit 10 years ago.
His oxygen saturation is 93% on room air.
On physical examination, he has fine end-inspiratory crackles at the lung bases and digital clubbing.
The patient undergoes a chest x-ray as part of the initial evaluation.
Pulmonary function testing shows a decreased total lung capacity and a reduced diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide.

encounters.cc: Rapidly growing nodule on right forearm for 3 months

lines: Rapidly growing nodule on right forearm for 3 months
The 74-year-old male with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and history of basal cell carcinoma presents to Dermatology.
He reports that the lesion began as a small, painless bump but has since increased to 2 cm in diameter.
He denies any bleeding or pruritus but notes a central area of crusting.
- Basal Cell Carcinoma (Nodular type, of nose) (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
Extensive sun exposure, 30-pack-year smoking history, although he quit 10 years ago
On physical examination, the nodule is dome-shaped with a central keratin-filled crater and surrounding erythema.
A biopsy of the lesion is performed, and histopathology shows well-differentiated squamous cells with minimal atypia and a central keratin core.

encounters.cc: Painless jaundice and unintentional weight loss

lines: Painless jaundice and unintentional weight loss
The patient with progressive idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and skin malignancies presents with painless jaundice.
He reports a significant loss of appetite and weight loss of 10 kg over the same period.
He denies any abdominal pain, fever, or changes in bowel habits.
- Basal Cell Carcinoma (Nodular type, of nose) (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
30-pack-year smoking history, although he quit smoking 10 years ago
On physical examination, the patient appears cachectic and has a palpable, nontender gallbladder.
Abdominal ultrasound shows dilated intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts with no evidence of gallstones.
A mass is noted at the head of the pancreas.
